desc:
A grid contains these cells: 0 is always open, 1 is a wall, 2 is a gate that is open only during even minutes, and 3 is a gate that is open only during odd minutes.

At minute 0 you stand on the top-left cell. In every minute you either stay where you are or move to one of the four adjacent cells. The cell you stand on at minute t must be open at minute t. So you cannot enter a gate while it is closed, and you also cannot stay on a gate when it closes.

Return the earliest minute at which you can stand on the bottom-right cell, or -1 if you never can.

grid = [[0,3,0],
        [1,1,2]]

result = 4      (minute 1: (0,1); minute 2: (0,2); minute 3: wait, the gate below is closed; minute 4: (1,2))
hints: Time matters, but a gate only cares whether the current minute is even or odd. How many different 'time states' does a cell really have?
Use BFS on states (cell, parity of the current minute). From a state at minute t you can go to the same cell or a neighbour at minute t + 1, if the target cell is open at that minute.

The goal is reached when any state at the bottom-right cell is first discovered; the layer number at that moment is the minute. Reaching a state later with the same parity can never be better, so each (cell, parity) is expanded once.
editorial: The future of a walker depends only on its cell and on whether the minute is even or odd, because the gates repeat every two minutes. That gives at most 2 × rows × cols states. Each BFS layer is one minute: from every state of layer t - 1 try staying and the four moves, and keep a candidate when the target cell is open at minute t (type 0, type 2 at even t, type 3 at odd t) and the pair (cell, t mod 2) is new.

Why is discarding a repeated (cell, parity) correct? If the walker could stand there at minute t and again at t + 2k, every plan that starts at the later time can be started 2k minutes earlier, because the gate pattern is the same. So the earliest visit dominates.
The first layer that contains the bottom-right cell is the answer (minute 0 if the grid is a single cell). If the frontier becomes empty, return -1. The total cost is O(rows × cols).
